name: tmux
summary: Terminal multiplexer: persistent sessions, windows and split panes, a scriptable status line, key tables and a plugin ecosystem via TPM.
startupCostMs: Server start is a few ms on Linux/macOS; it adds one pane process layer. Status line formats that call `#(shell command)` run every status-interval seconds, so keep them cheap. Not measurable on this Windows machine (no native tmux).

windows.notes: No official or native Windows build (tmux needs a POSIX pty). Options: run it inside WSL (use the Linux entry) or use Zellij, which has native Windows builds since 0.44. A third-party tmux-style multiplexer for Windows exists (psmux: winget `marlocarlo.psmux` 3.4.0, scoop `psmux`, ships a tmux.exe alias); it is not tmux, and config/plugin (TPM) compatibility was not verified here.

macos.notes: validate parses the file without executing it (`source-file -n`, per the tmux wiki) on a throwaway socket; the argv was not run here (no tmux on this machine) and the exit code on a parse error is unverified. Needs `tmux-256color` terminfo: if tmux says 'missing or unsuitable terminal', `brew install ncurses` or fall back to screen-256color.

linux.notes: tmux reads /etc/tmux.conf, then ~/.tmux.conf, ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf (XDG path since 3.2). Prebuilt static binaries: https://github.com/tmux/tmux-builds. After upgrading tmux run `tmux kill-server` (the protocol version changes between releases).

plugins.notes: TPM (tmux plugin manager) installs git-hosted plugins.
